- handoff: End-of-session handoff. Reconcile the project's tracking file (mark done resolved, promote every leftover to a live item with value+trigger, log decisions/debt/lessons), verify green via the project's oracle command, confirm nothing lives only in chat or a disposable note, persist a disposable resume prompt (with a cold-start reload list of the links that mattered this session) into the tracking file, checkpoint-commit, then compact the note. Project-agnostic. Use when wrapping up, pausing, "prep handoff", "close the session", or "generate a resume prompt".
- linkedin-review: Multi-agent parallel review of a LinkedIn profile against benchmarks, via Playwright MCP browser navigation. Spawns N specialized personas (decideur-client, commercial-esn, personal-branding, concurrent-freelance, copywriter, ats-keywords, seo-linkedin) in parallel, each producing an independent critique. Returns a synthesized report with convergences, conflicts, prioritized actions. Use when the user asks to audit/review their LinkedIn profile.
- review-plan: Multi-agent parallel review of a plan, design doc, or architecture proposal. Spawns N expert personas (product, security, performance, seo, devex, cloud-architecture, finops, compliance, accessibility) in parallel, each producing an independent critique. Returns a synthesized report with convergences, conflicts, and decisions to make. Use when the user asks to review a plan, audit a design, get multiple perspectives on a doc, or run a "multi-agent review".
- rtk: RTK (Rust Token Killer) proxy meta-commands. Use when the user asks for RTK token-savings analytics, command history, missed-opportunity discovery, or wants to bypass the auto-rewrite hook (rtk proxy). The PreToolUse hook auto-rewrites Bash commands transparently - do not invoke this skill for normal commands.
- add-contact: Create one CRM Contact via add-contact.py (deterministic, schema-validated). Use when adding a person with optional Org affiliations. For multi-entity free text, use add-lead.
- add-editorial-carousel: Generate a branded LinkedIn carousel (document post) for a piece from the BGA carousel skeleton. Composes N portrait 4:5 pages from the piece narrative (Why/How/What) using page-type primitives (cover, bullets, term, flow, compare, synth, cta - §5.8 catalogue), renders each page for a legibility gate, runs brand-review, delivers a swipeable PDF, wires it back into the piece `## Visuels`. Use when the user wants a carousel, a document post, or a live retex repurposed as swipeable pages.
- add-editorial-idea: Capture a new editorial idea (LinkedIn post, article, talk seed) as an anchor in `02-Areas/Éditorial/Ideas/`. Runs dedup check, applies frontmatter schema, enforces BGA brand conformity, updates MoC. Auto-detects express vs standard mode. Use when the user wants to capture, add, save, or register an editorial idea, post idea, article idea, or content seed.
- add-editorial-piece: Transform an editorial anchor (`Ideas/<file>.md`) into a piece for a given format (linkedin, article, live, podcast, talk). Resolves the anchor, fills frontmatter from template SSoT, drafts the body, runs brand conformity, ticks the matching line in the anchor's Déclinaisons checklist. Use when the user wants to draft a LinkedIn post, article, talk, live, or podcast piece from an existing idea.
- add-editorial-slides: Generate a branded HTML slide deck for a piece from the BGA slides skeleton. Composes slides from the piece narrative (Why/How/What, key points, tables) using slide-type primitives (title, bullets, cards, table, flow, callout, def, compare, probe, layers - §5.7 catalogue) selected per idea via the §5.7 archetype heuristic, renders each slide for a legibility gate, runs brand-review, wires the deck back into the piece. Interactive HTML opened in the browser, no delivery PNG. Use when the user wants intro slides, a live deck, or a talk/workshop deck for an editorial piece.
- add-editorial-visual: Generate a branded editorial visual (square post visual or LinkedIn event banner) for a piece from the BGA HTML skeleton. Reads the piece's `## Visuels` brief (format + disposition + setup/Why + contenu/How + synthèse/What), composes with CSS auto-layout (never hand-placed coordinates), renders HTML->PNG via Playwright, gates on visual legibility + brand-review, wires the asset back into the piece. Use when the user wants a schema, diagram, before/after, lifecycle visual, or event banner for a LinkedIn post, article, or live.
- add-formation: Bootstrap a new BGA formation by aggregating N editorial anchors (`Ideas/*.md`) into a curriculum. Creates the formation folder, generates the index from template, scaffolds one module file per anchor, backlinks each anchor via its Déclinaisons checklist, updates the Formations MoC. Supports direct mode (--ideas arg) or interactive mode (anchor picker grouped by pillar). Use when the user wants to create, scaffold, build, or initialize a training, workshop, masterclass, or curriculum.
- add-interaction: Create one CRM Interaction (dated exchange report) via add-interaction.py (deterministic, schema-validated). Use to log a call/meeting/email/event tied to an Opp or Org.
- add-lead: Add a new prospect (Organisation + optional Opportunity + optional Contact) to the CRM. Accepts free text and/or LinkedIn URLs. Use when the user mentions a new company or contact to add.
- add-opportunity: Create one CRM Opportunity via add-opp.py (deterministic, schema-validated). Use when adding a new channel/deal on an existing or new target Org. One Opp = one channel.
- add-organisation: Create one CRM Organisation via add-org.py (deterministic, schema-validated). Use when adding a single company (no opportunity/contact). For multi-entity free text + LinkedIn, use add-lead.
- archive-opportunity: Move a closed CRM Opportunity (perdu/gagne) to Opportunities/_archive/ via archive-opp.py (git mv, FK-safe). Use to declutter active pipeline after a deal closes.
- archive-project: Guided PARA archival of a finished project. Extracts forward-looking artefacts BEFORE the move - active backlog to Projects, living doc/SSoT to an existing or newly-created Area, structural decisions to ADRs, pure reference to Resources - sets the frozen marker, git mv to 04-Archives, propagates orphan wikilinks. Judgment-heavy (classify + route); writes = git mv + targeted edits. Use when a project is done and must be archived.
- brand-review: Audit a BGA editorial artifact (text and/or visual) against brand SSoT. Verifies tone-of-voice principles, format specs, color tokens, WCAG ratios, text/visual coherence. Outputs a status table + one prioritized recommendation.
- parse-td-results: Parse a Tutorial Dojo HTML exam result, extract incorrect questions, and append summaries to the AWS SAP Mistakes note.
- synthesize-interaction: Synthesize a freelance prospection Interaction draft - restructure the raw note and propagate to the linked Opportunity/Organisation. Thick orchestrator - LLM synthesis only, writes delegated to deterministic scripts.
- update-contact: Update an existing CRM Contact via update-contact.py (deterministic, schema-validated, idempotent). Set personal fields, append Org affiliations or notes.
- update-lead: Quick update of an existing Organisation or Opportunity from free text (informal conversation, phone call, ad-hoc info). Auto-detects the target. Use when the user reports info about an existing prospect.
- update-opportunity: Update an existing CRM Opportunity (non-status fields) via update-opp.py (deterministic, schema-validated, idempotent). For status/lost/won transitions use transition-opp.
- update-organisation: Update an existing CRM Organisation via update-org.py (deterministic, schema-validated, idempotent). Set durable company fields or append to body regions.
- weekly-actions: Display prospection actions for the current calendar week (Mon-Sun), including overdue items. Source - Opportunities. Use when the user asks for actions, planning, or prospection to-do.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

name: BGA editorial - tournure positive par défaut
description: Préférence éditoriale BGA Consulting - formuler en affirmatif, éviter "pas de", "ne plus", "sans", négations multiples. Codifié en principe 2.7 du tone of voice.
type: feedback

Toute production éditoriale BGA Consulting (posts LinkedIn, articles, mails, slides, docs client) doit privilégier les tournures affirmatives. Éviter "pas de X", "ne plus", "sans", négations multiples. Dire ce qu'on fait / protège / rend possible plutôt que ce qu'on évite.

**Why** : marque posée et exigeante, pas alarmiste. Une marque conseil rassure par ce qu'elle construit, pas par ce qu'elle bannit. Le négatif fatigue à la lecture longue et signale une posture défensive. Demande explicite Baptiste 2026-05-10.

**How to apply** :
- Reformuler systématiquement les phrases négatives en affirmatif lors de toute rédaction ou relecture BGA.
- Exception assumée : listes Do/Don't, anti-positions du brief, règles bloquantes (WCAG FAIL, em-dash interdit, etc.) - le négatif y joue un rôle de frontière.
- Codifié dans `02-Areas/BGA Consulting/Brand/05-Tone-of-voice.md` section 2.7.
- Lors d'une passe validation sur un texte BGA, traiter ce critère au même titre que les coquilles et le fact-check.

# Live - Terraform actions hors CRUD

## Accroche

Live technique, démos réelles dans le repo. Jeudi 30 juillet, 13h. LinkedIn + Twitch.

Promesse : Terraform 1.14 fait entrer l'impératif dans le déclaratif. Le bloc `action` déclenche le day-2 (invalidation de cache, backup, job) depuis le lifecycle, en natif : visible au plan, exécuté par le provider. On le met à l'épreuve en direct sur deux démos AWS.

## Corps

### Conducteur - Terraform passe à l'action (live S31, jeu. 2026-07-30)

Sujet direct (décision 2026-07-27, sans sondage - pool ADR-009 ouvert pour la suite). Démos = labs publics `examples/terraform-actions` (PR #27, CloudFront) et `examples/terraform-actions-lambda` (PR #28, Lambda/DynamoDB) sur [bgauduch/terraform-examples](https://github.com/bgauduch/terraform-examples). Découplage intact : le repo ne référence jamais ce live.

Public : praticiens IaC et équipes plateforme qui portent du day-2 en scripts autour de Terraform. Héros : le **bloc `action`** (le mécanisme), pas les ressources des démos. Scène : terminal + navigateur (site CloudFront, console DynamoDB), micro-deck 3 slides max. Arc : **WHY (le day-2 vivait hors du plan) → WHAT teaser (action + action_trigger) → HOW x2 (action native · échappatoire Lambda) → limites honnêtes → close**.

Durée : ≤ 1h, cœur ~38 min + Q&A généreuse. Registre « on » participatif (tone 2.10).

#### Idée-force du live : le day-2 rentre dans le plan
Jusqu'ici l'impératif post-provisioning (invalider un cache, sauvegarder avant mutation, lancer un job) vivait dans des `null_resource` + `local-exec` : hors plan, dépendant du CLI et des credentials ambiants, erreurs opaques. Le bloc `action` (v1.14, GA) le déclare : le *quoi* dans `action`, le *quand* dans `action_trigger` du lifecycle. La preuve au plan, l'exécution par le provider.

#### Conducteur timé (~38 min cœur + Q&A)

##### 13h00-13h04 · WHY (S0, slide)
- Le constat : Terraform excelle au CRUD, le day-2 débordait en scripts hors plan. Cas vécus : invalidation CDN au déploiement, backup avant mutation.
- L'histoire du sujet : capacité présentée au vote de juin, restée sur le banc ; ses démos attendaient en PR, on les joue aujourd'hui.
- Versions posées d'entrée (fact-check) : `action` **v1.14, GA** ; events `before/after_create|update` uniquement ; destroy = v1.16 **alpha**, à venir - jamais « dispo ».

##### 13h04-13h07 · WHAT teaser (S1, slide)
- Le couple : `action` déclare le *quoi* (config provider), `lifecycle.action_trigger` branche le *quand* (events). Schéma une ligne : event → action → side-effect prouvé.
- 4 actions AWS natives à date : `aws_lambda_invoke`, `aws_cloudfront_create_invalidation`, `aws_codebuild_start_build`, `aws_ec2_stop_instance`.

##### 13h07-13h20 · HOW-A action native : CloudFront (T1, lab PR #27)
- Visite du lab : bucket S3 privé (OAC) + distribution CloudFront + `index.html` ; `action_trigger` events `[after_create, after_update]` → `aws_cloudfront_create_invalidation`.
- Infra pré-appliquée (pre-flight) : le site répond, « Content version: v1 ».
- **Le geste** : modifier `content/index.html` (v2) → `terraform apply` → l'action apparaît au plan, l'invalidation part, le site sert v2 immédiatement (pas d'attente TTL).
- Le why face à `local-exec` : dans le plan, credentials du provider, erreurs lisibles, événements réels du lifecycle.

##### 13h20-13h33 · HOW-B l'échappatoire : Lambda + DynamoDB (T2, lab PR #28)
- Les actions natives sont rares → `aws_lambda_invoke` exécute **tout ce qu'une Lambda sait faire**. Ici : backup on-demand horodaté de la table à chaque create/update.
- **Le geste** : modifier un attribut de la table → apply → `aws dynamodb list-backups` montre le nouveau backup. Filet de sécurité déclaratif.
- Bonus fort : `terraform apply -invoke=action.aws_lambda_invoke.backup` - l'action à la demande, zéro changement d'infra.
- Subtilité d'architecte : le cycle de dépendance évité (IAM de la Lambda scopé sur un ARN construit, jamais sur la table). Aparté : une action native `aws_dynamodb_create_backup` existe ; la Lambda démontre le mécanisme générique - préférer le natif quand il couvre.

##### 13h33-13h38 · Limites honnêtes + horizon (S2, slide)
- Events create/update only : le cas « cleanup/snapshot avant destroy » attend les events destroy d'`action_trigger`, **v1.16 alpha** ([CHANGELOG](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)). À présenter « à venir », jamais dispo - dernière stable 1.15.x.
- Couverture provider naissante (4 actions AWS) ; l'échappatoire Lambda comble.
- Quand rester en CI/pipeline : orchestrations multi-systèmes, longues, avec approbations. L'action = side-effect court, couplé au lifecycle d'UNE ressource.

##### 13h38-13h40 · CLOSE
- Recap : le quoi (`action`), le quand (`action_trigger`), la preuve (plan + invalidation + backup).
- Repo + PRs en commentaire, pool de sujets ouvert pour le prochain live. → Q&A.

##### 13h40-14h00 · Q&A
- Amorces : « quel day-2 vit encore en script chez vous ? », « qui a déjà fait un local-exec dont il a honte ? » (auto-dérision, on l'a tous fait).

#### Pre-flight (mer. 29/07 soir + jeu. avant 13h)
- **Appliquer les 2 labs la veille** (CloudFront met 5-15 min à déployer : jamais en direct) ; vérifier site v1 + premier backup listé. Les applies du live = updates uniquement (rapides).
- Pin toolchain : `mise` → terraform 1.14.9 par lab (fait, commit d'alignement). Sandbox : région **eu-west-1** (SCP region-lock S3).
- Branches à jour : PRs #27 (`5dadc45`) / #28 (`0b31048`) rebasées sur main, CI verte, MERGEABLE. Démos jouées depuis les branches ; merge = à la main de Baptiste, hors live.
- Onglets : PRs #27/#28, doc `invoke-actions`, CHANGELOG 1.14, console CloudFront + DynamoDB (backups).
- Terminal police 18-20px, thème clair ; fallbacks : screenshots plan/invalidation/backups si réseau capricieux.

#### Pros / cons (à énoncer franchement)
**Pros** : l'impératif entre dans le plan (visible, review-able) ; credentials provider (rien d'ambiant sur le runner) ; events réels du lifecycle ; `-invoke` pour l'à-la-demande.
**Cons** : GA récent, couverture provider mince ; events destroy absents (v1.16 alpha) ; pas un remplaçant de la CI pour les orchestrations longues.

## CTA

Repo public à l'écran (`bgauduch/terraform-examples`, PRs #27/#28 en 1er commentaire). VOD en suivi. Échange : Calendly.

Calendly qualification : https://calendly.com/baptiste-gauduchon/linkedin-echange-qualification-de-besoin

=== CLAUDE.md ===
# AGENTS.md

Guidance for AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, OpenAI Codex, Aider, etc.) working in this repository. A `CLAUDE.md` symlink points here so Claude Code picks it up automatically. Each example also has its own nested `AGENTS.md` with example-specific guidance - read it before editing inside an example.

## What this repo is

A **library of self-contained Terraform examples**. Each lives under `examples/<name>/` and is independent: its own `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, tooling (`mise.toml`, `.tflint.hcl`) and Terraform root module(s). Examples are **not** factored into shared code - isolation is intentional so each can be read, run, and live-demoed on its own.

Use cases served: reusable patterns, illustrations for blog/LinkedIn posts, and starting points / labs for live tech sessions.

## Taxonomy

Every example declares a primary `type` plus free-form tags. Source of truth is the catalogue table in the root `README.md`; each example's `README.md`/`AGENTS.md` restates its type.

- `pattern` - reusable, production-leaning reference.
- `lab` - starting point / TP with progressive steps for a live session.
- `experiment` - preview/RC features, may be intentionally unstable.

Do **not** create top-level category directories (`patterns/`, `experiments/`...). Keep `examples/` flat and classify via `type` + tags. This avoids lifecycle churn when an example changes category.

## How to add an example (golden path)

1. `mkdir examples/<name>/` - kebab-case, scope-first (`aws-multi-env`, `terraform-rc-variables`).
2. Add `README.md` (state its `type` + tags, objective, run steps) and `AGENTS.md` (example-specific guidance).
3. Add per-example tooling: `mise.toml` (pins `terraform`, may be an RC/prerelease for `experiment` types; inherits `tflint`/`trivy` from the repo-root `mise.toml`) and `.tflint.hcl`.
4. Add the Terraform root module(s). Any directory containing a `providers.tf` is auto-discovered by CI - no CI edit needed to validate it.
5. Register a row in the root `README.md` catalogue table.

## CI

`.github/workflows/terraform.yml` auto-discovers Terraform root modules (directories containing `providers.tf`) under `examples/` and runs `validate` + `tflint` + `trivy` per module in a matrix. `terraform fmt -check -recursive` runs once at the root. The `tf-setup` composite action installs the toolchain via `jdx/mise-action` from the target module's merged `mise.toml` (terraform, tflint, trivy). Adding an example requires no CI change.

## Toolchain (mise)

[mise](https://mise.jdx.dev/) is the **single source of truth (SSOT)** for every CLI tool, locally and in CI - there is no separate version file or per-tool CI setup step.

- **Root `mise.toml`** pins repo-wide tools (`tflint`, `trivy`) plus a default `terraform`. **Per-example `mise.toml`** overrides only `terraform` (versions legitimately differ per example) and inherits the rest, since mise merges every `mise.toml` from the cwd up to the repo root.
- **Add a new tool once, in `mise.toml`** (root if repo-wide, example if local). Never re-pin a tool as a CI input - CI installs whatever `mise.toml` declares.
- **Renovate** bumps these via its native `mise` manager; alpha/beta/rc pins (e.g. `experiment` examples) are frozen by a `packageRule` matching `currentValue`.
- **Tasks replace Makefiles**: run with `mise run <task>`, list with `mise tasks`. Each task runs in a subshell, so a task's `cd` (or `dir`) never leaks into your interactive shell.
- **Locally**: `mise install` once, then tools resolve automatically per directory (use `mise exec -- <cmd>`, or activate mise in your shell).

## Repository standards

- **Language**: English everywhere in committed content - code, comments, identifiers, docs, `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, script output strings. No other language, including inside an example. (This repo is read on screen and public; mixed languages stand out.)
- **Git flow**: GitHub flow (short-lived feature branches off `main`, PR review, squash-merge). Name branches `<type>/<kebab-summary>` where `<type>` is a Conventional Commit type (`feat`, `fix`, `build`, `ci`, `docs`, `chore`, `refactor`, `test`) - e.g. `build/mise-toolchain-ssot` - so branch names stay consistent with commit messages and PR titles.
- **Work tracking**: durable backlog = GitHub Issues + Milestone (a goal + its acceptance criteria); each PR references its issue (`Closes #N`). `main` carries no task file - session plans stay local/ephemeral. `tasks/lessons.md` holds durable repo lessons.
- **Commit messages**: [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) - `<type>(<scope>): <subject>`. Use the example name as scope when relevant (e.g. `feat(aws-multi-env): ...`).
  - Common types: `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `chore`, `refactor`, `test`, `ci`, `build`.
  - Breaking changes: append `!` after type/scope or add a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer.
  - Keep subject imperative, lowercase, no trailing period, ~72 chars max.
  - Enforced in CI: `commitlint.yml` (commit messages, config-conventional) and `pr-title.yml` (semantic PR title, since squash-merge uses the PR title).
- **Versioning**: [SemVer](https://semver.org/), repo-level single release line via release-please.
- **Validation before commit**: `terraform fmt -recursive` (root) and `terraform validate` inside each touched root module. Optional local mirror of the CI gates lives in `.pre-commit-config.yaml` (fmt/validate/tflint + conventional commit-msg); enable with `pre-commit install --install-hooks && pre-commit install --hook-type commit-msg`.

content.content:
name: Commit messages

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]

concurrency:
  group: commitlint-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  lint:
    name: Conventional commits
    # Bot branches (dependabot, release-please) carry machine-generated commit bodies that get
    # discarded on squash-merge; their conventional-commit contract on `main` is enforced by the
    # Semantic PR title check instead. Skip per-commit linting to avoid noise on bot PRs.
    if: >-
      github.actor != 'dependabot[bot]' &&
      !startsWith(github.ref_name, 'release-please--')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6.0.3
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: wagoid/commitlint-github-action@b948419dd99f3fd78a6548d48f94e3df7f6bf3ed # v6.2.1
=== tasks/ ===
lessons.md  3.4K
# Repo lessons

Durable lessons learned while working in this repository. Append new entries; keep them short and actionable.

## CI

- **Trivy single-scan + convert** - run `trivy config . --format json --output trivy.json --exit-code 0` once, then drive both the report and the gate from that one JSON with `trivy convert`: `--severity MEDIUM,HIGH,CRITICAL --exit-code 0` for visibility and `--severity HIGH,CRITICAL --exit-code 1` to block. Scanning once and converting twice keeps a single source of truth and avoids re-scanning per severity. The `trivy` CLI is installed by `mise` (pinned in the repo-root `mise.toml`), so the raw `trivy` commands are available in the step - no separate `setup-trivy`/`trivy-action`.

## Security hardening

- **KMS rotation (`AWS-0065`)** - `trivy config` flags `aws_kms_key` without `enable_key_rotation = true`. Always enable rotation on customer-managed keys; pair it with a deliberately short `deletion_window_in_days` (AWS minimum is 7) only in throwaway demos, with a comment explaining why.
- **S3 versioning (`AWS-0090`)** - an encrypted, private bucket still trips the scanner without an `aws_s3_bucket_versioning` resource set to `Enabled`. Versioning is a separate resource, not an inline block on `aws_s3_bucket`.
- **Variable validation** - mark required inputs `nullable = false` and add a `validation {}` block (region regex, `cidrhost()` for CIDRs, `contains()` allow-lists for enums). Failures then surface at plan time with a clear message instead of as opaque provider errors at apply.
- **Documented exceptions** - low-value scanner findings that would bloat a teaching example (S3 access logging `AWS-0089`, VPC flow logs `AWS-0178`) are documented in the example README rather than silenced with inline ignores.

## Dependency management

- **mise is the toolchain SSOT** - terraform, tflint and trivy versions live in `mise.toml` (repo root for shared tools, per-example for the `terraform` override), never in `.terraform-version` files or per-tool CI inputs. mise merges every `mise.toml` from the cwd to the repo root, so an example only restates what it changes. CI installs them via `jdx/mise-action`; locally `mise install` + `mise exec`/`mise run` resolve the right versions per directory.
- **Renovate's native `mise` manager** bumps the tools in `mise.toml` automatically - no custom manager needed for them. Keep a regex `customManager` only for versions that still live in action inputs (e.g. the `# renovate: datasource=github-releases depName=jdx/mise` annotation pinning the mise CLI in `tf-setup`). Freeze intentional RC/alpha pins (the `experiment` examples) with a backend-agnostic `packageRule` on `matchCurrentValue: "/-(alpha|beta|rc)/"` (match the value, not the dep name, since the mise backend may report a different `depName`).
- **mise + air-gapped/policy-restricted networks** - mise's `aqua` backend verifies tflint/trivy via cosign + GitHub artifact attestations, which reach `sigstore.dev`/`tuf-repo-cdn.sigstore.dev`; a `terraform` exact pin instead downloads straight from HashiCorp (no sigstore). If a sandbox blocks sigstore, exact-version installs of aqua tools fail there even though GitHub-hosted CI succeeds - it is an egress limitation, not a config defect.

# Repo lessons

Durable lessons learned while working in this repository. Append new entries; keep them short and actionable.

## CI

- **Trivy single-scan + convert** - run `trivy config . --format json --output trivy.json --exit-code 0` once, then drive both the report and the gate from that one JSON with `trivy convert`: `--severity MEDIUM,HIGH,CRITICAL --exit-code 0` for visibility and `--severity HIGH,CRITICAL --exit-code 1` to block. Scanning once and converting twice keeps a single source of truth and avoids re-scanning per severity. The `trivy` CLI is installed by `mise` (pinned in the repo-root `mise.toml`), so the raw `trivy` commands are available in the step - no separate `setup-trivy`/`trivy-action`.

## Security hardening

- **KMS rotation (`AWS-0065`)** - `trivy config` flags `aws_kms_key` without `enable_key_rotation = true`. Always enable rotation on customer-managed keys; pair it with a deliberately short `deletion_window_in_days` (AWS minimum is 7) only in throwaway demos, with a comment explaining why.
- **S3 versioning (`AWS-0090`)** - an encrypted, private bucket still trips the scanner without an `aws_s3_bucket_versioning` resource set to `Enabled`. Versioning is a separate resource, not an inline block on `aws_s3_bucket`.
- **Variable validation** - mark required inputs `nullable = false` and add a `validation {}` block (region regex, `cidrhost()` for CIDRs, `contains()` allow-lists for enums). Failures then surface at plan time with a clear message instead of as opaque provider errors at apply.
- **Documented exceptions** - low-value scanner findings that would bloat a teaching example (S3 access logging `AWS-0089`, VPC flow logs `AWS-0178`) are documented in the example README rather than silenced with inline ignores.

## Dependency management

- **mise is the toolchain SSOT** - terraform, tflint and trivy versions live in `mise.toml` (repo root for shared tools, per-example for the `terraform` override), never in `.terraform-version` files or per-tool CI inputs. mise merges every `mise.toml` from the cwd to the repo root, so an example only restates what it changes. CI installs them via `jdx/mise-action`; locally `mise install` + `mise exec`/`mise run` resolve the right versions per directory.
- **Renovate's native `mise` manager** bumps the tools in `mise.toml` automatically - no custom manager needed for them. Keep a regex `customManager` only for versions that still live in action inputs (e.g. the `# renovate: datasource=github-releases depName=jdx/mise` annotation pinning the mise CLI in `tf-setup`). Freeze intentional RC/alpha pins (the `experiment` examples) with a backend-agnostic `packageRule` on `matchCurrentValue: "/-(alpha|beta|rc)/"` (match the value, not the dep name, since the mise backend may report a different `depName`).
- **mise + air-gapped/policy-restricted networks** - mise's `aqua` backend verifies tflint/trivy via cosign + GitHub artifact attestations, which reach `sigstore.dev`/`tuf-repo-cdn.sigstore.dev`; a `terraform` exact pin instead downloads straight from HashiCorp (no sigstore). If a sandbox blocks sigstore, exact-version installs of aqua tools fail there even though GitHub-hosted CI succeeds - it is an egress limitation, not a config defect.
- **Validate before merge** - `npx --package renovate renovate-config-validator .github/renovate.json` catches schema errors locally; the Mend app uses the in-repo config (no onboarding PR) once present.

# AGENTS.md - terraform-actions-lambda example

Guidance for AI coding agents working inside this example. Repo-wide conventions live in the root
`AGENTS.md`; this file covers what is specific to `terraform-actions-lambda`.

Taxonomy: **type `lab`** - progressive, playable in a live session. Tags: `aws`, `actions`,
`lambda`, `dynamodb`, `v1.14`.

## Purpose and scope

A **pedagogical demo** (live tech session, 30-45 min). It shows Terraform 1.14 actions used as
a **generic escape hatch**: `action "aws_lambda_invoke"` runs arbitrary logic (here a DynamoDB
on-demand backup) on a resource lifecycle event. Companion to `terraform-actions`, which uses a
native provider action.

Keep it minimal and focused on the action → Lambda mechanism. Do not swap the Lambda for the native
`aws_dynamodb_create_backup` action: going through Lambda is the whole lesson (call it out, do not
"optimise" it away).

## Architecture

Single root module (`providers.tf` is auto-discovered by CI). Flow:

`aws_dynamodb_table.this` → `lifecycle.action_trigger` → `action "aws_lambda_invoke".backup` →
`aws_lambda_function.backup` (+ IAM role/policy, log group, zipped `lambda/backup.py`).

**Cycle avoidance (important):** the Lambda must not depend on the table, or
`table → action → lambda → table` becomes a cycle that `terraform validate` rejects. The IAM policy
scopes `dynamodb:CreateBackup` to `local.table_arn` (built from `var.region` + caller account id +
table name), never `aws_dynamodb_table.this.arn`. Keep it that way.

## Common commands

```bash
terraform init
terraform apply                 # after_create -> first backup
# change a table attribute, then:
terraform apply                 # after_update -> new timestamped backup
terraform apply -invoke=action.aws_lambda_invoke.backup   # stand-alone, on-demand backup
terraform destroy
```

Validation before committing: `terraform fmt -recursive` (root) and `terraform validate` here.

## Prerequisites

- Terraform `>= 1.14.0` (pinned to `1.14.9` in `mise.toml`).
- AWS provider `6.41.0` (carries the `aws_lambda_invoke` action); `archive` provider zips the Lambda.
- AWS credentials for `apply`; default region `eu-west-1`.

## Conventions in this example

- `events` are bare identifiers (`after_create`, not `"after_create"`).
- IAM is least-privilege: `dynamodb:CreateBackup` on the table ARN, logs to the function's own group.
- The Lambda zip lands in `build/` (git-ignored) via the `archive_file` data source.
- Tags via `local.common_tags` (`Project` / `ManagedBy`); follow the same shape for new resources.

}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The table whose lifecycle triggers the backup on create and on update.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
resource "aws_dynamodb_table" "this" {
  name         = local.table_name
  billing_mode = "PAY_PER_REQUEST"
  hash_key     = "id"

  attribute {
    name = "id"
    type = "S"
  }

  point_in_time_recovery {
    enabled = true
  }

  server_side_encryption {
    enabled = true
  }

  ttl {
    attribute_name = "expires_at"
    enabled        = true
  }

  tags = local.common_tags

  lifecycle {
    action_trigger {
      events  = [after_create, before_update]
      actions = [action.aws_lambda_invoke.backup]
    }
  }
}

name: Commit messages

# Scoped to `pull_request`, not `push`: on a push the action lints the
# `before..after` range, which after a rebase or force-push spans commits already
# merged into `main` (release-please bodies carry a >100-char bot trailer) and
# fails a PR that only contains conforming commits. On `pull_request` the range is
# `base..head`, i.e. exactly the commits the PR proposes.
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]

concurrency:
  group: commitlint-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  lint:
    name: Conventional commits
    # Bot branches (dependabot, release-please) carry machine-generated commit bodies that get
    # discarded on squash-merge; their conventional-commit contract on `main` is enforced by the
    # Semantic PR title check instead. Skip per-commit linting to avoid noise on bot PRs.
    if: >-
      github.actor != 'dependabot[bot]' &&
      !startsWith(github.head_ref, 'release-please--')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6.0.3
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: wagoid/commitlint-github-action@b948419dd99f3fd78a6548d48f94e3df7f6bf3ed # v6.2.1

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# Repo lessons

Durable lessons learned while working in this repository. Append new entries; keep them short and actionable.

## CI

- **Trivy single-scan + convert** - run `trivy config . --format json --output trivy.json --exit-code 0` once, then drive both the report and the gate from that one JSON with `trivy convert`: `--severity MEDIUM,HIGH,CRITICAL --exit-code 0` for visibility and `--severity HIGH,CRITICAL --exit-code 1` to block. Scanning once and converting twice keeps a single source of truth and avoids re-scanning per severity. The `trivy` CLI is installed by `mise` (pinned in the repo-root `mise.toml`), so the raw `trivy` commands are available in the step - no separate `setup-trivy`/`trivy-action`.

## Security hardening

- **KMS rotation (`AWS-0065`)** - `trivy config` flags `aws_kms_key` without `enable_key_rotation = true`. Always enable rotation on customer-managed keys; pair it with a deliberately short `deletion_window_in_days` (AWS minimum is 7) only in throwaway demos, with a comment explaining why.
- **S3 versioning (`AWS-0090`)** - an encrypted, private bucket still trips the scanner without an `aws_s3_bucket_versioning` resource set to `Enabled`. Versioning is a separate resource, not an inline block on `aws_s3_bucket`.
- **Variable validation** - mark required inputs `nullable = false` and add a `validation {}` block (region regex, `cidrhost()` for CIDRs, `contains()` allow-lists for enums). Failures then surface at plan time with a clear message instead of as opaque provider errors at apply.
- **Documented exceptions** - low-value scanner findings that would bloat a teaching example (S3 access logging `AWS-0089`, VPC flow logs `AWS-0178`) are documented in the example README rather than silenced with inline ignores.

## Dependency management

- **mise is the toolchain SSOT** - terraform, tflint and trivy versions live in `mise.toml` (repo root for shared tools, per-example for the `terraform` override), never in `.terraform-version` files or per-tool CI inputs. mise merges every `mise.toml` from the cwd to the repo root, so an example only restates what it changes. CI installs them via `jdx/mise-action`; locally `mise install` + `mise exec`/`mise run` resolve the right versions per directory.
- **Renovate's native `mise` manager** bumps the tools in `mise.toml` automatically - no custom manager needed for them. Keep a regex `customManager` only for versions that still live in action inputs (e.g. the `# renovate: datasource=github-releases depName=jdx/mise` annotation pinning the mise CLI in `tf-setup`). Freeze intentional RC/alpha pins (the `experiment` examples) with a backend-agnostic `packageRule` on `matchCurrentValue: "/-(alpha|beta|rc)/"` (match the value, not the dep name, since the mise backend may report a different `depName`).
- **mise + air-gapped/policy-restricted networks** - mise's `aqua` backend verifies tflint/trivy via cosign + GitHub artifact attestations, which reach `sigstore.dev`/`tuf-repo-cdn.sigstore.dev`; a `terraform` exact pin instead downloads straight from HashiCorp (no sigstore). If a sandbox blocks sigstore, exact-version installs of aqua tools fail there even though GitHub-hosted CI succeeds - it is an egress limitation, not a config defect.
- **Validate before merge** - `npx --package renovate renovate-config-validator .github/renovate.json` catches schema errors locally; the Mend app uses the in-repo config (no onboarding PR) once present.

input.command:
gh pr create --base main --head ci/commitlint-pr-scope --title "ci(commitlint): lint PR commits, not the push range" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Why

Both open action labs (#27, #28) are red on `Conventional commits` while every commit they contain conforms. The `push` event makes `wagoid/commitlint-github-action` lint the `before..after` range; after a rebase that range spans commits already merged into `main`, and the release-please release commits carry a `Co-authored-by: github-actions[bot] <...>` trailer over the 100-char `footer-max-line-length`. A PR is then failed for history it does not own.

## What

Switch the trigger to `pull_request`, where the action lints `base..head` - exactly the commits the PR proposes. `github.ref_name` becomes `github.head_ref` for the release-please skip. Job name unchanged, so branch protection keeps matching.

Lesson recorded in `tasks/lessons.md`.

## Verification

This PR is its own test: the check runs on the `pull_request` event and passes on a branch that would previously have been linted against the push range.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -3

Le DNS local (routeur `10.0.1.1`) intercepte le port 53 et renvoie `0.0.0.0` pour tout nom commençant par `logs.`, dont `logs.<region>.amazonaws.com` (règle de filtrage anti-tracker). Constaté 2026-07-28 en préparant les démos du live S31.

**Symptôme** : `dial tcp 0.0.0.0:443: connect: connection refused` sur n'importe quel appel CloudWatch Logs (création/refresh d'un `aws_cloudwatch_log_group`, `aws logs ...`). Le reste d'AWS passe normalement (dynamodb, lambda, s3, cloudfront, monitoring).

**Diagnostic en 2 commandes** : `dig +short logs.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com` renvoie `0.0.0.0`, alors que la même requête en DoH renvoie une IP publique :
`curl -s -H 'accept: application/dns-json' 'https://cloudflare-dns.com/dns-query?name=logs.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com&type=A'`
Le test `dig @1.1.1.1` ne suffit pas à trancher : le routeur intercepte aussi les requêtes vers les résolveurs publics, donc il répond `0.0.0.0` lui aussi. Seul le DoH (port 443) contourne l'interception.

**Contournement immédiat** : `export AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_CLOUDWATCH_LOGS=https://logs.eu-west-1.api.aws` (le nom dual-stack `*.api.aws` résout normalement ; les SDK AWS ne basculent pas dessus tout seuls). **Correctif durable** : whitelister l'endpoint sur le routeur, ou passer en partage de connexion mobile.

Vérifier ce point avant toute démo live impliquant Lambda, ECS ou quoi que ce soit qui crée un log group. Voir [[reference_aws_sandbox_scp_region]] pour les autres contraintes du compte sandbox.

Terminé. Les deux démos sont opérationnelles, répétées bout-en-bout, et CI verte partout.

## Ce qui était cassé

| # | Problème | Statut |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | CI rouge sur #27 et #28 (`commitlint` lintait la plage de push, qui après rebase embarquait des commits de `main`) | Corrigé à la racine, PR #38 |
| 2 | **La copy promettait « backup avant que la table bouge », le lab déclenchait sur `after_update`** (donc après) | Corrigé : `before_update` |
| 3 | Geste live démo 2 non défini (« modifier un attribut ») | Défini : décommenter le bloc `ttl`, 10s |
| 4 | Aucun `.terraform.lock.hcl` dans les 2 labs (16 ailleurs dans le repo) | Ajoutés |
| 5 | DNS local qui blackhole `logs.*.amazonaws.com` | Diagnostiqué, **action de ta part requise** |

## L'histoire à raconter (le vrai gain)

Les deux démos ne sont plus « une action native + une échappatoire Lambda », elles illustrent **les deux familles d'événements** : `after_*` publie une conséquence du changement (l'invalidation suit la mise en ligne), `before_*` protège contre le changement (le backup existe pendant que la table est encore dans son état d'avant). Un seul mécanisme, deux métiers du day-2. À l'écran, `Action complete` **puis** `Modifying...` : la démonstration se fait toute seule.

## Mesures de répétition (dans le conducteur)

- Invalidation CloudFront : **37s**, l'apply attend la propagation → à meubler en lisant les lignes de l'action à voix haute (et ajouté aux cons : une action longue rallonge chaque apply).
- Geste TTL : **10s** (mutation 5s). J'ai testé un index secondaire d'abord : **8min42** de `Still modifying...`, écarté.
- Création distribution : 2min42 → pre-flight la veille confirmé.

## À faire de ton côté

1. **Whitelister `logs.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com` sur le routeur** (`10.0.1.1` renvoie `0.0.0.0`, règle anti-tracker sur `logs.`). Sans ça **tout apply de la démo 2 échoue**, même un refresh. Contrôle : `dig +short logs.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com` doit rendre une IP publique. Secours validé : `export AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_CLOUDWATCH_LOGS=https://logs.eu-west-1.api.aws`.
2. **Merger les 3 PRs** ou pas, à ton choix (le conducteur dit hors live).

Toute production éditoriale BGA Consulting (posts LinkedIn, articles, mails, slides, docs client) doit privilégier les tournures affirmatives. Éviter "pas de X", "ne plus", "sans", négations multiples. Dire ce qu'on fait / protège / rend possible plutôt que ce qu'on évite.

**How to apply** :
- Reformuler systématiquement les phrases négatives en affirmatif lors de toute rédaction ou relecture BGA.
- Exception assumée : listes Do/Don't, anti-positions du brief, règles bloquantes (WCAG FAIL, em-dash interdit, etc.) - le négatif y joue un rôle de frontière.
- Codifié dans `02-Areas/BGA Consulting/Brand/05-Tone-of-voice.md` section 2.7.
- Lors d'une passe validation sur un texte BGA, traiter ce critère au même titre que les coquilles et le fact-check.

=== S30 (live précédent) - refs slides dans le conducteur ===
38:Public : praticiens Cloud/DevOps et responsables d'équipe qui portent (ou hésitent à porter) un projet OSS. Héros : le **process du repo** (Renovate + release-please + CI + gouvernance + framework agents), pas l'image Docker elle-même. Scène : GitHub + terminal local, quasi sans slides. Arc : **WHY (l'histoire) → WHAT teaser (la release sans clavier) → HOW x3 (industrialiser · guider · encadrer les agents) → WHAT cap (monorepo) → close**.
46:`S` slide · `G` GitHub (navigateur) · `T` terminal

Base directory for this skill: /Users/bgauduch/Obsidian Vault/.claude/skills/add-editorial-slides

# Add Editorial Slides

Generate a branded HTML slide deck (interactive, browser-first) for a piece. Distinct artifact class from PNG visuals (§5.0): multi-slide, responsive 16:9, delivered as-is (opened in the browser). The skeleton fixes the frame + slide-type components; Claude assembles **semantic slides**, never absolute coordinates. A **legibility gate by per-slide inspection** + brand-review lock the result. Content FR.

## SSoT - read at runtime, never restate

| Concern | Source |
|---|---|
| Slides format spec (slide-types catalogue, layout, navigation) | `02-Areas/BGA Consulting/Brand/03-Design-system.md` §5.7 |
| Format registry (dims, naming, home) | `03-Design-system.md` §5.0 |
| Color tokens + WCAG ratios | `03-Design-system.md` §1.1 / §1.2 |
| Executable skeleton (frame + slide-type classes + slot markers + nav) | `02-Areas/BGA Consulting/Brand/skeletons/slides.html` |
| HTML->PNG renderer (QA, supports `?slide=N`) | `02-Areas/BGA Consulting/Brand/_pipeline/render-html.mjs` |
| Voice (positive phrasing §2.7, Golden Circle arc §2.9) | `02-Areas/BGA Consulting/Brand/05-Tone-of-voice.md` |
| Asset naming, piece link, lint gate | `02-Areas/Éditorial/CLAUDE.md` |

Reverse-engineering from an existing deck is forbidden (BGA CLAUDE.md Asset production contract). The skeleton is the only structural base.

## Input

`--piece <path>` (required). Source = the piece body: `## Accroche` (hook), `## Corps` (Why → How → What), key bullets, tables.
`--scope intro|full` (optional, default `intro`): `intro` = short deck (~5 slides: title, context/Why, key cases or points, one synthesis table, transition); `full` = cover the conductor.
`--out <path>` (optional): override output; default `02-Areas/Éditorial/assets/slides-<subject>.html`.

## Workflow

### 1. Read the piece + outline the deck
- Read the piece. Extract: the hook (`## Accroche`), the Why → How → What spine, key bullets, any tables (reuse **verbatim** as `table` slides).
- Build a slide list: pick a slide-type per idea via the **§5.7 archetype heuristic** (content→format table, read at runtime). Catalogue, archetypes and heuristic live in §5.7 only - never restate the mapping here. `intro` scope: keep ~5 slides. Positive phrasing (§2.7), one idea per line, Golden Circle arc (§2.9).
- Lead slide = `title` (piece H1 + a key fragment in `<span class="hl">` + a framing `sub`). Close = `flow` or a `title` transition ("place à la suite").

### 2. Clone the skeleton
- Copy `Brand/skeletons/slides.html` → `<out>` (default `02-Areas/Éditorial/assets/slides-<subject>.html`, `<subject>` kebab-case from the piece). Collision → suffix `-2` and warn.

### 3. Fill the slides region (semantic HTML, never coordinates)
- Replace content between `<!-- slot:slides:start -->` / `<!-- slot:slides:end -->` (markers only, never line numbers). Missing/orphan marker → explicit abort, no fallback.
- One `<section class="slide">` per slide, first one `active`. Use the skeleton's component classes per slide-type (§5.7). **Add `.slide-logo` (wordmark top-right) on every slide except `title`** (the cover carries the big wordmark) - the skeleton reference slides show the markup. Reuse the piece's tables as-is for `table` slides; emphasise the key cell with `class="em"` and the last row is auto-highlighted.
- Compose HTML that lays itself out (no fixed heights/positions; text must wrap). Keep each slide concise to fit the frame - the engine does not shrink the font; split a dense slide in two rather than overflow.

### 4. Legibility gate (per slide, blocking)
- For each slide N: `node "02-Areas/BGA Consulting/Brand/_pipeline/render-html.mjs" "<out>?slide=N" /tmp/<subject>-<N>.png 1280 720`, then **Read the PNG**. Check: no overlap, no text outside its frame or truncated, legible hierarchy (kicker < h1/h2), the slide fits. Any anomaly → fix the HTML (concision, split), re-render. The PNG is authoritative, not the HTML.

### 5. Brand-review gate
- Run the `brand-review` skill: `--visual <out> --visual-png <representative slide PNG> --text <piece>`.
- Pre-check: `grep -oE '#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}' <out> | sort -u` ⊆ whitelist §1.1.
- Verdict ≠ PRÊT (incl. V9 legibility) → fix, re-render, re-review. Steps 4+5: max 3 loops, then surface the residual.

### 6. Wire the piece (idempotent)
- In `## Notes production`, add/refresh one line pointing to the deck: ``Deck de slides : `assets/slides-<subject>.html` (ouvrir au navigateur ; flèches / clic, `f` plein écran).`` Re-run with the same deck = no-op. Slides are a live-support artifact, not a `## Visuels` PNG entry - keep them out of the `## Visuels` brief.
- Run `python3 02-Areas/Éditorial/scripts/lint-editorial.py --file <piece> --apply`; report residual violations.

### 7. Return
- Deck path. Slide count + slide-types used. Legibility gate: OK | fixed (n loops). Brand-review verdict (+ manual residuals). Piece wiring: applied | already present.

## Rules
- Skeleton = structural SSoT. No reverse-engineering of existing decks; changing the frame or slide-types = amend §5.7 + the skeleton first.
- **Layout delegated to CSS**: never absolute positioning, never hand-computed coordinates. Compose semantic slides with the skeleton classes.
- Tokens = closed whitelist §1.1. Missing color → STOP, amend the design-system.
- Text on light background respects WCAG §1.2. `#C68A14` decorative only (bars, arrows).
- Interactive HTML is the deliverable; the PNG is QA-only (no delivery PNG). An illegible slide is never delivered, even if tokens/WCAG pass.
- One deck = one `slides-<subject>.html` (§5.0, home `Éditorial/assets/`, ADR-006).
- Output FR; English limited to this SKILL.md.

## 5. Imagerie et photo

### 5.0 Registre des formats de visuel

SSoT unique du tuple par-format. Les autres docs (CLAUDE.md, skill, templates, ADR, §5.4/5.5/5.6) **pointent ici**, ne réénoncent jamais dims/squelette/nommage.

| format | dimensions | ratio | spec | type |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `square` | 1200x1200 | 1:1 | §5.4 | éditorial (par-pièce) |
| `event-banner` | 1600x900 | 16:9 | §5.6 | éditorial (par-pièce) |
| `stream-scene` | 1920x1080 | 16:9 | §5.5 | brand (réutilisable) |
| `capture` | source fournie | - | §5.3 | éditorial (par-pièce, `nature: capture`) |
| `slides` | responsive 16:9 | 16:9 | §5.7 | éditorial (par-pièce, HTML interactif) |
| `carousel` | 1080x1350 | 4:5 | §5.8 | éditorial (par-pièce, multi-page PDF) |

Règles dérivées, valables pour tous les formats (énoncées **une seule fois**) :
- **Squelette** = `Brand/skeletons/<format>.html` (dérivé de la clé ; `capture` = source externe, sans squelette).
- **Nommage instance** = `<format>-<sujet>.{html,png}` : le format **est** le préfixe et **dérive** les dimensions (jamais dans le nom ; rendu @2x).
- **Home** des instances par-pièce = `02-Areas/Éditorial/assets/` (ADR-006). Les formats réutilisables (`stream-scene`) vivent dans leur famille `Brand/`.
- **Enum** des formats éditoriaux validés (`square`, `event-banner`) : `02-Areas/Éditorial/enums.yml` clé `visual-format`, lue par le linter.
- **`slides`** = deck HTML interactif (multi-slides), livré tel quel au navigateur : aucun PNG de livraison (le PNG sert seulement au gate QA via `?slide=N`). Nommage `slides-<sujet>.html`. Vocabulaire de slide-types et navigation : §5.7. Hors enum `visual-format` (réservée aux visuels PNG éditoriaux).
- **`carousel`** = carrousel LinkedIn (document post) : N pages portrait 4:5, livré en **PDF** `carousel-<sujet>.pdf` (le post document EST le carrousel). Source `carousel-<sujet>.html` ; PNG par page = **transient** (gate QA via `?page=N` + input du PDF), jamais persisté dans `assets/`. Vocabulaire de page-types et arc narratif : §5.8. **Dans** l'enum `visual-format` (c'est le visuel d'une pièce `linkedin`), contrairement à `slides`. Assemblage PDF : `_pipeline/render-pdf.mjs`.

Hors périmètre §5 : bannière profil (1584x396) et OG (1200x630) → [[06-Roadmap-declinaisons]].

### 5.1 Photo professionnelle (portrait Baptiste)

- Recadrage 1:1 obligatoire pour avatars (LinkedIn, signature, monogramme contextuel)
- Recadrage 3:4 ou 4:5 pour portraits éditoriaux (page À propos, headers article)
- Traitement colorimétrique : chaleur légère (+5 à +10 sur balance) pour cohérence avec la palette ambre, sans virage orange marqué
- Fond neutre crème ou désaturé proche de `--color-bg`, jamais de fond blanc pur ni noir
- Contraste préservé sur le visage : éviter les ombres dures, lumière diffuse type fenêtre

### 5.2 Imagerie de support

À privilégier :
- Artisanat et outils : établi, atelier, mains au travail (pas en gros plan sur clavier)
- Matière et texture : bois, papier, métal patiné, cuir, béton brut
- Contexte de travail réel : tableau blanc dessiné main, post-its, schémas papier
- Photographies d'architecture industrielle calme (silos, tuyauterie, charpente) en métaphore d'infrastructure

À proscrire :
- ❌ Stock photo générique tech (équipe en open space souriante devant écran)
- ❌ Néon, cyan fluo, dark mode dominant
- ❌ Hands-on-keyboard cliché
- ❌ Cloud illustré comme un nuage rebondi de cartoon
- ❌ Code défilant sur écran noir style Matrix

### 5.3 Schémas et diagrammes

- Fond : `--color-surface` ou `--color-bg`
- Traits : `--color-text-primary` 1.5px
- Accents et flux mis en avant : `--color-accent`
- États : tokens success / warning / danger
- Police : Manrope 14px pour labels, JetBrains Mono 12-14px pour valeurs techniques

### 5.4 Visuel de post éditorial (carré)

Format de déclinaison des visuels qui accompagnent un post (schéma, avant/après, cycle de vie). Format, dims, squelette, nommage : §5.0. Source HTML -> PNG en auto-layout CSS (rendu Playwright sur `document.fonts.ready`) ; pipeline de rendu documenté dans `02-Areas/BGA Consulting/CLAUDE.md` (Asset pipelines), hors périmètre design. Le HTML/CSS est imposé pour que la géométrie (positions, tailles, wrap) soit gérée par le moteur de layout, jamais à la main : c'est ce qui garantit l'absence de collision/débordement. Squelette = **1 cadre générique partagé + primitives transverses + recettes de disposition** (une par archétype, ajoutée à la demande, jamais en dupliquant le cadre).

=== §5.7 ===
### 5.7 Deck de slides (HTML interactif)

Deck de slides d'appui (intro de live, talk, atelier), affiché en direct au navigateur. Classe distincte des visuels PNG : multi-slides, responsive 16:9, navigable. Format, nommage, home, squelette : §5.0. Filière HTML auto-layout CSS (jamais de coordonnée à la main) ; assemblage du contenu par le skill `add-editorial-slides`.

**Nature** : un seul fichier HTML, N slides, une visible à la fois. Livré tel quel (ouvert au navigateur) ; le PNG sert uniquement au gate de légibilité (via `?slide=N`). Aucun PNG de livraison.

**Catalogue des slide-types** (primitives du squelette, analogues aux dispositions §5.4) :
| slide-type | usage |
|---|---|
| `title` | ouverture : kicker + titre (fragment `hl`) + sous-titre + wordmark |
| `bullets` | 2-3 idées, une par ligne (libellé `<b>` + phrase) ; puces visibles optionnelles via `.puces` (marqueur accent décoratif) |
| `cards` | 3-4 cas parallèles, une carte par colonne |
| `table` | synthèse dense, lecture progressive (dernière ligne surlignée) |
| `flow` | suite d'étapes `step → step`, transition |
| `callout` | encart définition/note dense **inline**, attaché au contenu (« Terme ? … »). Lead-in `warning`, corps `muted` |
| `def` | définition détachée en **aside** bas de slide (`.slide-def` : pleine largeur, alignée gauche, au-dessus du chrome de nav, 1 ligne par idée). Informe sans surcharger le bloc principal. Distinct de `callout` (inline vs aside détaché) |
| `compare` | 2 silhouettes en regard + flèche, axes partagés optionnels ; largeur de bande = volumétrie. Bibliothèque de silhouettes nommées : `sil-pyramid`, `sil-diamond`. Bande `.hot` = aplat `accent` + texte indigo (blanc-sur-accent INTERDIT §1.2) |
| `probe` | transition + sondage chat / CTA discret (mesurer l'intérêt en live) |
| `layers` | carte de strates / couches empilées : positionnement dans une stack ; une bande par couche ; `.opt` (bordure pointillée) = couche optionnelle ; `.chip` (accent-soft) = surligner une couche ; `.note` (warning) = caption latérale |

**Archétypes** (presets = combinaisons de slide-types par intention ; ce que le skill compose par défaut, recombinable en blocs libres hors-moule) :
| intention de la slide | archétype | slide-types |
|---|---|---|
| ouvrir / fermer / transition | title | `title` (+ `probe` si CTA/sondage) |
| affirmer + preuves | claim+bullets | `bullets` (+ `callout` si un terme à définir) |
| définir une notion | definition | `bullets` court + `def` (aside détaché `.slide-def` ; `callout` inline si la déf doit rester collée au contenu) |
| comparer deux états / avant-après / transformation | comparison | `compare` (+ `callout` légende) |
| départager des options | landscape | `table` |
| progression / pipeline / couches | pipeline | `flow` (+ `lead`) |
| cartographier / positionner en couches | layers | `layers` |

**Heuristique de sélection** (contenu → format, le sélecteur, pour trancher sans aller-retour) : partir du rôle rhétorique de l'idée (Why/How/What) et de sa forme. Une notion → `definition` · deux états → `comparison` · un éventail d'options → `landscape` · une suite d'étapes → `pipeline` · un empilement de couches / un positionnement dans une stack → `layers` · une affirmation + preuves → `claim+bullets` · une transition/sondage → `title`/`probe`.

**Layout** : fond `--color-bg` crème + motif pointillé `indigo-soft` 22px (signature partagée), barre accent `--color-accent` en haut à gauche. Échelle typo responsive (`clamp`), bloc centré verticalement, marges ≥ 6vh / 9vw. Wordmark `wordmark-color-light` (logo/sources/) sur la slide `title` (ancre d'identité, co-branding [[04-Logo]] §5) ; sur **toutes les autres slides**, wordmark compact `.slide-logo` (BGA · Consulting) en haut à droite, la barre accent restant à gauche.

**Navigation** : flèches / clic (gauche-droite) / espace ; plein écran touche `f` ; compteur de slides. Gate QA : `?slide=N` affiche la slide N seule, chrome masqué.

**Tokens / police** : Manrope (titres, labels), JetBrains Mono (kicker, identifiants techniques). Ambre `#C68A14` décoratif uniquement (filets, barres, flèches), jamais en texte. Texte sur aplats `bg` / `surface` only, WCAG §1.2. Tokens §1.1 = whitelist fermée.

**Assets** : nommage, home et squelette → §5.0 (type éditorial par-pièce, ADR-006). Génération : skill `add-editorial-slides`.

- **Nommage instance** = `<format>-<sujet>.{html,png}` : le format **est** le préfixe et **dérive** les dimensions (jamais dans le nom ; rendu @2x).
- **Home** des instances par-pièce = `02-Areas/Éditorial/assets/` (ADR-006). Les formats réutilisables (`stream-scene`) vivent dans leur famille `Brand/`.
- **Enum** des formats éditoriaux validés (`square`, `event-banner`) : `02-Areas/Éditorial/enums.yml` clé `visual-format`, lue par le linter.
- **`slides`** = deck HTML interactif (multi-slides), livré tel quel au navigateur : aucun PNG de livraison (le PNG sert seulement au gate QA via `?slide=N`). Nommage `slides-<sujet>.html`. Vocabulaire de slide-types et navigation : §5.7. Hors enum `visual-format` (réservée aux visuels PNG éditoriaux).
- **`carousel`** = carrousel LinkedIn (document post) : N pages portrait 4:5, livré en **PDF** `carousel-<sujet>.pdf` (le post document EST le carrousel). Source `carousel-<sujet>.html` ; PNG par page = **transient** (gate QA via `?page=N` + input du PDF), jamais persisté dans `assets/`. Vocabulaire de page-types et arc narratif : §5.8. **Dans** l'enum `visual-format` (c'est le visuel d'une pièce `linkedin`), contrairement à `slides`. Assemblage PDF : `_pipeline/render-pdf.mjs`.

Hors périmètre §5 : bannière profil (1584x396) et OG (1200x630) → [[06-Roadmap-declinaisons]].

### 5.1 Photo professionnelle (portrait Baptiste)

- Recadrage 1:1 obligatoire pour avatars (LinkedIn, signature, monogramme contextuel)
- Recadrage 3:4 ou 4:5 pour portraits éditoriaux (page À propos, headers article)
- Traitement colorimétrique : chaleur légère (+5 à +10 sur balance) pour cohérence avec la palette ambre, sans virage orange marqué
- Fond neutre crème ou désaturé proche de `--color-bg`, jamais de fond blanc pur ni noir
- Contraste préservé sur le visage : éviter les ombres dures, lumière diffuse type fenêtre

### 5.2 Imagerie de support

À privilégier :
- Artisanat et outils : établi, atelier, mains au travail (pas en gros plan sur clavier)
- Matière et texture : bois, papier, métal patiné, cuir, béton brut
- Contexte de travail réel : tableau blanc dessiné main, post-its, schémas papier
- Photographies d'architecture industrielle calme (silos, tuyauterie, charpente) en métaphore d'infrastructure

À proscrire :
- ❌ Stock photo générique tech (équipe en open space souriante devant écran)
- ❌ Néon, cyan fluo, dark mode dominant
- ❌ Hands-on-keyboard cliché
- ❌ Cloud illustré comme un nuage rebondi de cartoon
- ❌ Code défilant sur écran noir style Matrix

### 5.3 Schémas et diagrammes

- Fond : `--color-surface` ou `--color-bg`
- Traits : `--color-text-primary` 1.5px
- Accents et flux mis en avant : `--color-accent`
- États : tokens success / warning / danger
- Police : Manrope 14px pour labels, JetBrains Mono 12-14px pour valeurs techniques

### 5.4 Visuel de post éditorial (carré)

Format de déclinaison des visuels qui accompagnent un post (schéma, avant/après, cycle de vie). Format, dims, squelette, nommage : §5.0. Source HTML -> PNG en auto-layout CSS (rendu Playwright sur `document.fonts.ready`) ; pipeline de rendu documenté dans `02-Areas/BGA Consulting/CLAUDE.md` (Asset pipelines), hors périmètre design. Le HTML/CSS est imposé pour que la géométrie (positions, tailles, wrap) soit gérée par le moteur de layout, jamais à la main : c'est ce qui garantit l'absence de collision/débordement. Squelette = **1 cadre générique partagé + primitives transverses + recettes de disposition** (une par archétype, ajoutée à la demande, jamais en dupliquant le cadre).

=== §5.7 ===
### 5.7 Deck de slides (HTML interactif)

Deck de slides d'appui (intro de live, talk, atelier), affiché en direct au navigateur. Classe distincte des visuels PNG : multi-slides, responsive 16:9, navigable. Format, nommage, home, squelette : §5.0. Filière HTML auto-layout CSS (jamais de coordonnée à la main) ; assemblage du contenu par le skill `add-editorial-slides`.

**Nature** : un seul fichier HTML, N slides, une visible à la fois. Livré tel quel (ouvert au navigateur) ; le PNG sert uniquement au gate de légibilité (via `?slide=N`). Aucun PNG de livraison.

**Catalogue des slide-types** (primitives du squelette, analogues aux dispositions §5.4) :
| slide-type | usage |
|---|---|
| `title` | ouverture : kicker + titre (fragment `hl`) + sous-titre + wordmark |
| `bullets` | 2-3 idées, une par ligne (libellé `<b>` + phrase) ; puces visibles optionnelles via `.puces` (marqueur accent décoratif) |
| `cards` | 3-4 cas parallèles, une carte par colonne |
| `table` | synthèse dense, lecture progressive (dernière ligne surlignée) |
| `flow` | suite d'étapes `step → step`, transition |
| `callout` | encart définition/note dense **inline**, attaché au contenu (« Terme ? … »). Lead-in `warning`, corps `muted` |
| `def` | définition détachée en **aside** bas de slide (`.slide-def` : pleine largeur, alignée gauche, au-dessus du chrome de nav, 1 ligne par idée). Informe sans surcharger le bloc principal. Distinct de `callout` (inline vs aside détaché) |
| `compare` | 2 silhouettes en regard + flèche, axes partagés optionnels ; largeur de bande = volumétrie. Bibliothèque de silhouettes nommées : `sil-pyramid`, `sil-diamond`. Bande `.hot` = aplat `accent` + texte indigo (blanc-sur-accent INTERDIT §1.2) |
| `probe` | transition + sondage chat / CTA discret (mesurer l'intérêt en live) |
| `layers` | carte de strates / couches empilées : positionnement dans une stack ; une bande par couche ; `.opt` (bordure pointillée) = couche optionnelle ; `.chip` (accent-soft) = surligner une couche ; `.note` (warning) = caption latérale |

**Archétypes** (presets = combinaisons de slide-types par intention ; ce que le skill compose par défaut, recombinable en blocs libres hors-moule) :
| intention de la slide | archétype | slide-types |
|---|---|---|
| ouvrir / fermer / transition | title | `title` (+ `probe` si CTA/sondage) |
| affirmer + preuves | claim+bullets | `bullets` (+ `callout` si un terme à définir) |
| définir une notion | definition | `bullets` court + `def` (aside détaché `.slide-def` ; `callout` inline si la déf doit rester collée au contenu) |
| comparer deux états / avant-après / transformation | comparison | `compare` (+ `callout` légende) |
| départager des options | landscape | `table` |
| progression / pipeline / couches | pipeline | `flow` (+ `lead`) |
| cartographier / positionner en couches | layers | `layers` |

**Heuristique de sélection** (contenu → format, le sélecteur, pour trancher sans aller-retour) : partir du rôle rhétorique de l'idée (Why/How/What) et de sa forme. Une notion → `definition` · deux états → `comparison` · un éventail d'options → `landscape` · une suite d'étapes → `pipeline` · un empilement de couches / un positionnement dans une stack → `layers` · une affirmation + preuves → `claim+bullets` · une transition/sondage → `title`/`probe`.

**Layout** : fond `--color-bg` crème + motif pointillé `indigo-soft` 22px (signature partagée), barre accent `--color-accent` en haut à gauche. Échelle typo responsive (`clamp`), bloc centré verticalement, marges ≥ 6vh / 9vw. Wordmark `wordmark-color-light` (logo/sources/) sur la slide `title` (ancre d'identité, co-branding [[04-Logo]] §5) ; sur **toutes les autres slides**, wordmark compact `.slide-logo` (BGA · Consulting) en haut à droite, la barre accent restant à gauche.

**Navigation** : flèches / clic (gauche-droite) / espace ; plein écran touche `f` ; compteur de slides. Gate QA : `?slide=N` affiche la slide N seule, chrome masqué.

**Tokens / police** : Manrope (titres, labels), JetBrains Mono (kicker, identifiants techniques). Ambre `#C68A14` décoratif uniquement (filets, barres, flèches), jamais en texte. Texte sur aplats `bg` / `surface` only, WCAG §1.2. Tokens §1.1 = whitelist fermée.

**Assets** : nommage, home et squelette → §5.0 (type éditorial par-pièce, ADR-006). Génération : skill `add-editorial-slides`.

# brand-review

Validate a BGA editorial artifact (LinkedIn post, blog draft, visual asset) against brand SSoT before publication.

## SSoT - read, never restate

| Concern | Doc |
|---|---|
| Voice, lexicon, principles 2.1-2.7, format §4.1, check-list §7 | `02-Areas/BGA Consulting/Brand/05-Tone-of-voice.md` |
| Color tokens §1.1, WCAG ratios §1.2, typo §2, components §6 | `02-Areas/BGA Consulting/Brand/03-Design-system.md` |
| Per-support specs (cadence, hook, hashtags, CTA, format) | `02-Areas/BGA Consulting/Brand/06-Roadmap-declinaisons.md` |
| Positioning, anti-positions, brand adjectives | `02-Areas/BGA Consulting/Brand/01-Brief.md` |

Inheritance: editorial CLAUDE.md (`02-Areas/Éditorial/CLAUDE.md`), incl. its per-channel publication tactics.

## Inputs

- `--visual "02-Areas/Éditorial/assets/slides-terraform-actions.html" --visual-png "/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-bgauduch-Obsidian-Vault/c3f6a54f-6fcd-455c-aa37-3c402e5a7edd/scratchpad/tfactions-3b.png" --text "02-Areas/Éditorial/Pieces/2026-07-27 Live - Terraform actions hors CRUD.md"` = one or two paths. Detect type by extension:
  - `.md` → text artifact
  - `.svg` / `.html` / `.png` → visual artifact
- If only one path: audit that dimension only.
- If both: also check text/visual coherence (same kicker, same key terms, no contradiction).
- If none: ask user for path(s).

## Workflow

1. Read inputs + the four SSoT docs above (relevant sections only).
2. Run text audit (if applicable).
3. Run visual audit (if applicable).
4. Run coherence check (if both).
5. Output status table + single prioritized recommendation.

## Text audit criteria

| # | Check | Pass condition |
|---|---|---|
| T1 | Principle 2.7 - tournure positive | Affirmative dominant; negative only for Do/Don't, anti-positions, blocking rules, idioms, external quotes |
| T2 | No em-dash | Zero `—` characters |
| T3 | Hook §4.1 | First 1-2 lines: chiffré or scénario concret, no buzzword opener |
| T4 | Structure §4.1 | Hook / Contexte / Insight / CTA discret ordering |
| T5 | CTA §4.1 | Discret ("je veux bien en discuter", "curieux de vos cas"), pas "DM-moi" |
| T6 | Lexicon §3.2 | Brand adjectives respected, anti-positions absent (hype, dark-tech-bro, corporate-consulting, jargon non explicité) |
| T7 | Hashtags | 3-5 max, on-topic |
| T8 | Anglais tech §3.3 | Identifiants réels (`AttachPolicy`, `SCP`, EventBridge) OK ; concept forgé → terme FR (gel sélectif, pas *blast hybride*) ; pas de franglais gratuit |
| T9 | Dates | Format `YYYY-MM-DD` partout |
| T10 | Check-list §7 | Tous les items applicables cochés |
| T11 | Arc narratif §2.9 | Golden Circle Why->How->What, ouverture sur tension/*pourquoi* ; pas d'outside-in (ouverture sur le *quoi*) ni liste sans fil |

## Visual audit criteria

| # | Check | Pass condition |
|---|---|---|
| V1 | Format §6 LinkedIn | 1200x1200 (carré) ou ratio support attendu |
| V2 | Background | `#FAF6EE` (cream) ou token surface autorisé |
| V3 | Color tokens §1.1 | Toutes les couleurs (grep des hex) ∈ whitelist `03-Design-system.md` §1.1 (lue au runtime, table sémantique complète : surfaces, texte, accent, border, états + soft). Hors-whitelist = échec |
| V4 | WCAG §1.2 | Chaque paire texte/fond respecte le ratio de `03-Design-system.md` §1.2 (lue au runtime). Ambre `#C68A14` décoratif uniquement, jamais texte (§7) |
| V5 | Typo §2 | Manrope pour titres/body, JetBrains Mono pour code/identifiants techniques |
| V6 | Hiérarchie | Kicker → H1 → H2 → body, weights conformes (kicker 600, h1 800, h2 700, body 400) |
| V7 | Logo / signature | Footer présent si support le requiert (`06-Roadmap-declinaisons.md`) |
| V8 | Accent bar | Top-left amber bar 80x4 (signature visuelle BGA) |
| V9 | Lisibilité / layout | **Inspection du PNG rendu** (Read sur le .png) : aucun chevauchement, aucun texte hors cadre ni tronqué, aucun élément superposé, hiérarchie lisible. Conformité tokens/WCAG ne vaut PAS validation visuelle. **Bloquant** : un visuel illisible n'est jamais PRÊT |
| V10 | Arc narratif (si setup) | Quand le brief prévoit un point de départ : ancrage *Why* (setup) + synthèse *What* présents, arc Why->How->What lisible (principe 2.9, §5.4) |

Tokens et ratios = SSoT `03-Design-system.md` §1.1 / §1.2, lues au runtime. Aucune valeur recopiée ici.

Points de vigilance (appliquer §1.2, ne pas deviner) :
- Texte d'état sur fond soft (success/warning/danger sur leur soft) : vérifier le seuil large/bold de §1.2 ; les petits labels/pills doivent atteindre la taille/graisse requise, sinon échec.
- **Ambre-sur-ambre** (warning/accent sur `accent-soft`/soft) = zone molle : contrôler le ratio §1.2 ou déplacer le complément sur fond crème (cf §5.4 bonus). Ne jamais présumer que ça passe.

## Coherence check (when both provided)

- Kicker visual == thèmes du texte
- H1/H2 visual reprend une phrase-clé du texte
- Étapes/garde-fous visuels alignés avec les bullets du texte
- Aucun terme dans le visuel qui n'apparaît pas dans le texte (et vice-versa pour les key terms)

## Output format

```
# Brand review - <artifact name(s)> - YYYY-MM-DD

## Texte
| # | Critère | Statut | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | Tournure positive | ✅/⚠️/❌ | <one-liner si non ✅> |
...

## Visuel
| # | Critère | Statut | Note |
...

## Cohérence texte/visuel (si applicable)
- ...

## Recommandation prioritaire
<une seule action, la plus impactante>

## Verdict
PRÊT / À RETOUCHER / À RETRAVAILLER
```

## Rules

- Read SSoT before judging; never invent specs.
- Cite section number (e.g., "§4.1", "principe 2.7") in notes.
- One recommendation max - the user picks one fix per round, not a backlog.
- French output (artifact language); English only inside this SKILL.md.
- If SVG: grep fills/strokes via `grep -oE '#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}'` to enumerate colors before judging V3/V4.
